meta.title: MD-SG
meta.subtitle: Multi-floor Open-vocabulary Online 3D Scene Graph with Dynamic Handling Navigation

shots.beat: Title over the hero clip's detection frame
shots.narration: MD-SG: object navigation with a scene graph that lets a map be wrong, notice, and recover.

shots.beat: The three-step protocol, on the real floor plates
shots.on_screen: layout_conditions panel (d): cracker box, table → kitchen island, 2.71 m of it vertical
shots.narration: That is the benchmark: map, move, search again with the old map, within a floor or across floors.

We formulate dynamic multi-floor object navigation, build an online open-vocabulary scene-graph pipeline that revises its object beliefs, and release the first benchmark with controlled same-floor and cross-floor relocation.

floors: floor 0 · two storeys below the mapped one
captions: open-vocabulary segmentation → ellipsoid tracks → floor · room · container · object
shots.beat: Perception to scene graph, on footage
shots.on_screen: detections + the scene-graph tree sliding in
shots.narration: Every detection is back-projected into an ellipsoid track and filed under floor, room and container. Stair edges join two storeys only after a traversal has actually completed.

captions: a mapped cracker-box track, p = 0.77 → approach it
inspect: the surface is in view and readable, and there is no box → eligible misses
absent on arrival: belief revised, the search moves on
shots.on_screen: belief bar dropping as the agent inspects an empty surface
shots.narration: A missed detection is not absence. A miss counts only when the object should have been visible; nearer depth means occlusion and no update. And the belief ceiling is low, so a few honest misses can overturn a long history.
That is the whole filter: one positive channel, one negative channel, and a third that refuses to count what it could not have seen.

captions: search mass favours the floor below → head for the stair flight the map already holds
events: floor score at step 13 · below: 4.55   here (mapped): 0.38 → go down
shots.beat: Belief-guided search and the floor decision, on footage
shots.narration: Every mapped surface carries a search posterior. The floor score is the mean over its surfaces, and every failed inspection multiplies belief down. The agent leaves a floor because what it has searched is spent, not because it saw something new.

shots.caption: scores cross after eight negative inspections; the switch is accepted after ten
shots.beat: Floor score panel (computed by the real code on 00873, query 'tin can')
shots.narration: A switch also needs a margin, and is held while a credible mapped track on this floor is still untested.

shots.caption: same episode · same prior map · the bottle was mapped upstairs, and is now downstairs
shots.beat: Hero: ours vs ASCENT on the identical episode
shots.on_screen: side by side, shared step clock, ours freezes on the detection
shots.narration: Same episode, same prior map. The bottle was mapped upstairs. MD-SG puts the search mass downstairs, takes the flight it already mapped, and finds the bottle in two hundred and seven steps. ASCENT, with the same map, never does.

captions: two flights down · cracker box · 282 steps · SPL 0.69
shots.narration: Down two flights.

captions: one flight up · yellow bottle · 292 steps · SPL 0.58
shots.narration: Up one.

captions: straight to the stairs · cracker box · 132 steps · SPL 0.53
shots.narration: Straight to the stairs.

captions: third climb attempt · cracker box · 789 steps · SPL 0.21
shots.narration: And across a building the map got wrong.
On the five-scene multi-floor benchmark ASCENT succeeds in none of twenty-five episodes; MD-SG in forty percent.

shots.beat: Table I cross-anchor + Table III trend
shots.narration: On DualMap's single-floor benchmark, cross-anchor success rises from thirty to fifty-three percent, and removing either belief mechanism costs eleven to seventeen points.

Revisable, floor-aware scene memory: a first-class design axis for navigation in buildings that change.
